title: Correctness of program compilation
statement: Let $P$ be a program, let $	ext{lim}$ specify word, space, and depth limits, let $p_0$ be a procedure index, and let $	ext{dec}$ be a Boolean. Suppose that the main call to procedure $p_0$, executed in $P$ at depth $0$ from the state whose local values are $(0,i,j)$ and whose memory is $�\mu$, reaches a state $�\sigma'$ with cost $c$. Suppose the word width $W$ satisfies $2(2\,\text{lim.word}+2)<2^W$, $2\,\text{lim.space}<2^W$, $4Q<2^W$ for $Q=\mathrm{stackCells}(P,\text{lim})$, and $2N<2^W$ for $N=\mathrm{dispPos}(P,\text{dec})$. Suppose also that the initial word-RAM memory represents $�\mu$ in every nonnegative cell, every value of $�\mu$ has absolute value at most $\text{lim.word}$, and its two argument cells contain $i$ and $j$, respectively, with $|i|,|j|\le\text{lim.word}$. Then running the compiled program from position $0$ for $\mathrm{ramSteps}(P,\text{dec},c)$ steps returns true exactly when $\text{dec}$ is false or $0<\sigma'.\mathrm{loc}(0)$. Moreover, some resulting word-RAM memory represents the final memory of $�\sigma'$ in every nonnegative cell, has $�\sigma'.\mathrm{loc}(0)$ in its result cell, preserves both argument cells, and agrees with the initial memory at every address below $-\mathrm{lowCell}(P,\text{dec},\text{lim})$ or at least $\text{lim.space$.}
hypotheses_covered: The main call executes at depth 0 from local values $(0,i,j)$ and memory $\mu$, reaching $\sigma'$ with cost $c$.
The initial memory represents $\mu$ in every nonnegative cell, and $|\mu(a)|\le\text{lim.word}$ for every natural-number address $a$.
The argument cells contain $i$ and $j$, and $|i|,|j|\le\text{lim.word}$.
replaced:
Let $P$ be a program, let $	ext{lim}$ be its limits, and let $i,j\\in\\mathbb{Z}$,
$\\mu:\\mathbb{N}\\to\\mathbb{Z}$, and $\\sigma'$ be a state. Suppose the light
execution of the main call to procedure $p_0$, starting at depth $0$ with local
variables $(0,i,j)$ and memory $\\mu$, ends in $\\sigma'$ with cost $c$. Suppose also
that the word size $W$ satisfies the compiler's fit conditions for the dispatcher
position and stack capacity, and that the initial word RAM memory represents $\\mu$ with
every memory value bounded in absolute value by $\\text{lim.word}$, and contains $i$ and
$j$ in the two argument cells, each bounded in absolute value by $\\text{lim.word}$.
Then running the compiled program from position $0$ for the prescribed number of steps
yields the verdict that is true exactly when either $\\text{dec}$ is false or the result
$\\sigma'.loc(0)$ is positive; moreover, there is a final word RAM memory whose ordinary
cells represent the final light memory, whose result cell contains $\\sigma'.loc(0)$,
whose argument cells are unchanged, and which agrees with the initial memory at every
address below the negative low-cell bound or at least the space limit.
